messages:
Marta: heads-up — nightly int8 rollout shows a subtle but consistent deterministic drop on our lm-eval sigset when longctx > 8k and KV cache reuse is high. seems correlated with aggressive slot coalescing + the int8 kernel path. anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:

Kevin: saw something similar in a smaller repro. suspect quantized slot merging creates slight alignment shifts that our int8 kernels then amplify. the fp16/bf16 path didn't move. :eyes:

Marta: attaching the quick profile dump I grabbed from the canary (shortened). curious about kernel selection + batching interplay.

Marta: ```
profile: kv_residency_histogram: [1200, 4500, 8200, 12000]
int8_error_rate: 0.73% (vs fp16 baseline 0.12%)
kernel_chosen: aten_fast_conv_int8 (92%), fallback: aten_conv_fp16 (8%)
batches_per_sec: 145 -> 160 when coalesce off
mem_growth_longctx: +1.4GB/1000 iters
```

Ryan: that mem_growth number jumps out — could be warmup/evict interplay where coalesced slots keep alive slightly different kv addresses, so our eviction LRU doesn't reclaim as expected. when residency distribution skews, int8 quantization noise matters more for recall.

Alex: sharing a tiny telemetry probe we used to get slot residency distribution. run on a canary:

Alex: ```py
# run in /internal/kvprobe
def residency_hist(samples):
    counts = Counter(s.slot_age for s in samples)
    return sorted(counts.items())
```

Kevin: actionable experiments: 1) force kernel selection to fp16 conv for a few hours (disable fast_int8 selector) and rerun evals; 2) disable slot coalescing on a subset of shards; 3) run with a slightly relaxed batching heuristic (max_batch_size -1) to see if fused kernels are sensitive to batch alignment.

Marta: I can toggle coalescing for 10% of traffic and flip kernel selector to prefer fp16 on same cohort. will schedule tonight.

perf-bot: regression-alert: lm-eval/sigset downward delta 0.61% at 2026-03-18T02:12Z. impacted cohorts: canary-int8-2, canary-int8-4. Related traces: link://perf/2360012345

Ryan: also check the paging telemetry — if compaction triggers during longctx sequences, pages may be rehydrated with slightly different quantization rounding due to sub-page ordering. that could explain deterministic skew.

Kevin: quick command to toggle kernel selector on a node pool:

Kevin: ```bash
curl -X POST https://internal-api/selector/toggle \
  -d '{"pool":"canary-int8-2","prefer":"fp16_conv"}' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

Marta: started experiment run at 2360012370 on shards 3-5 (10% traffic). disabling coalesce for those shards now. :thumbsup:

Alex: if we see accuracy recover but latency regresses, we should consider a mid-term fix: add a tiny deterministic jitter to slot placement during coalesce so quant rounding doesn't align badly across hot prefixes.

Kevin: agreed. also log the exact kernel micro-ops selection when we hit the eval cases (we need to see if a different matmul tile was chosen under int8 path).

Marta: results incoming — planning to collect 6h of traces and post summary here. thanks all. :pray:
